images.seen: A hadeda walking the dry verge of an empty Karoo-dorp street, white flat-roofed houses under an ominous dark storm sky. Monday.
lines: The street cleared out early; only the hadeda is finishing its rounds.
The sky is stacking up over the dorp and even the palm has gone still.

images.seen: An emergency vehicle with its lights on in a wet estate street strewn with downed branches, storm clearing into sunset behind. Saturday.
lines: The storm made one pass and left the street a week of gardening.
Branches down, lights on, storm gone: the after-party is all admin.
The sunset is back like nothing happened; the trees know otherwise.

images.seen: A young man on a high balcony at dusk filming a double lightning strike over the city, rain beading on the glass railing. Tuesday.
lines: Two strikes in one frame: the sky is doing his content for him.
Rain on the railing, lightning on the horizon, phone doing its best.
That strike will look half this size on the phone, and he knows it.

images.seen: A boy wrapped in a fleece blanket at the bedroom window, watching a lightning bolt come down over the suburb at night. Wednesday.
lines: First storm he has stayed up for, and the sky is making it count.
Thunder is scary from bed and magnificent from a window; he moved.
The best television in the house is currently the weather.
